steps.name: Glaucus
steps.text: Hm, tests completed. Everything's running normally.

steps.name: Glaucus
steps.text: And we'll be done once I install the Originium battery set. Where did that go...?

steps.name: Glaucus
steps.text: Hm?

steps.name: Glaucus
steps.text: Professor Millais?
Professor who?

steps.name: Glaucus
steps.text: Sorry, I got the wrong person. I thought only Professor Millais would come here around this time.
Oh...
You're the only one here. Is this... Raythean Industries' workshop?

steps.name: Glaucus
steps.text: Looks like it. That's what the sign said when I walked in.
You... understand all this high-tech stuff?

steps.name: Glaucus
steps.text: Well... A little?
Yo, I got a weapon made by you guys that's broken. Think you can fix it?

steps.name: Glaucus
steps.text: You want to get your weapon fixed?

steps.name: Glaucus
steps.text: (Why did his tone change all of a sudden?)
Can you do it?

steps.name: Glaucus
steps.text: (Not even a third of the time I have for this practical exam has passed. Maybe they noticed I finished early and decided to give me a new test?)

steps.name: Glaucus
steps.text: (So aside from design and modification, you also need to know how to make repairs... Becoming a Raythean equipment designer isn't easy, is it?)
What are you spacing out for? Can you do it or not?

steps.name: Glaucus
steps.text: I should be able to. What do you need fixed?

steps.name: Glaucus
steps.text: (He's even pretending to be a real customer. Is he evaluating my performance, too?)
Here.
The warranty card is in the bag, probably at the bottom, under everything.

steps.name: Glaucus
steps.text: It says Gordon... Are you Mr. Gordon?

steps.name: Gordon
steps.text: Yes.

steps.name: Glaucus
steps.text: Whoa... I've never seen a weapon like this before.

steps.name: Glaucus
steps.text: It looks like a regular crossbow from the outside, but the whole firing mechanism was overhauled. It's connected to... an EMG sensor!

steps.name: Glaucus
steps.text: It uses multiple EMG sensors to form a module recognition system that helps users with hand disabilities control the weapon. The design is genius.

steps.name: Glaucus
steps.text: When you wield it, you just need to lift the weapon to the right height, and the sensor module on your upper arm will be able to detect your muscles' movements.

steps.name: Glaucus
steps.text: So by moving their arm, the user can issue commands to control the crossbow's power and firing mechanism. Once they've gotten the hang of it, they could even fire it with no hands whatsoever.

steps.name: Glaucus
steps.text: ...With this design, you could definitely factory-produce weapons for disabled soldiers.

steps.name: Gordon
steps.text: Heh.

steps.name: Gordon
steps.text: It's those factories that gave me this dud. The EMG sensor you're talking about's broken.

steps.name: Glaucus
steps.text: Is it broken? I just plugged it in for a test. It should be working fine.

spans.text: it broken? I just plugged it in for a test. It should be working fine.

steps.name: Gordon
steps.text: Sometimes it works, sometimes it doesn't. If that's not broken, what is?

steps.name: Glaucus
steps.text: But the test signal...

steps.name: Gordon
steps.text: I don't need to know how it goddamn works! All this high tech stuff goes right over my head. Just fix it!

steps.name: Gordon
steps.text: And you better not slack off! I'm telling you I need it back this morning! If I don't get it back...

steps.name: Glaucus
steps.text: Don't worry. Debugging is very simple. It won't take all morning. You can watch me tune it.

steps.name: Glaucus
steps.text: Or you could sit somewhere. I'll be done in no time.

steps.name: Gordon
steps.text: ...Alright.

steps.name: Gordon
steps.text: Uh, about your legs...

steps.name: Glaucus
steps.text: Huh? You mean my exoskeleton?

steps.name: Glaucus
steps.text: I've got bad legs. It's thanks to these babies that I can walk.

steps.name: Gordon
steps.text: What happened?

steps.name: Glaucus
steps.text: It's genetic.

steps.name: Gordon
steps.text: So you need to wear those braces all the time... Isn't it painful?

steps.name: Glaucus
steps.text: I mean, it's definitely not the same as using your own legs, but I'm used to it.

steps.name: Gordon
steps.text: Doesn't Raythean have lots of high tech wheelchairs or whatever? They got those ones that can carry people and run around, or even give you a massage...

steps.name: Gordon
steps.text: You could just get one of those. It's gotta be better than putting up with how heavy that metal doohickey is, right?

steps.name: Glaucus
steps.text: A wheelchair would be more comfortable, but that only gives you mobility.

steps.name: Gordon
steps.text: Is that not enough?

steps.name: Glaucus
steps.text: I like the feeling of being able to stand up.

steps.name: Glaucus
steps.text: Don't get me wrong, a good mobility tool is great, but to me, my exoskeleton is irreplaceable.

steps.name: Glaucus
steps.text: The solid sensation you get from under your feet... How you get propelled forward by the ground when you run... The winds whispering in your ear...

steps.name: Glaucus
steps.text: I was thrilled by all the sensations throughout my body when I first walked on the ground with my own two feet.

steps.name: Glaucus
steps.text: It made me truly realize that, instead of floating powerlessly at the mercy of the wind, I'm... actually connected to the land.

steps.name: Glaucus
steps.text: Er, sorry for going off on a weird tangent. Pretend I never said that.

steps.name: Gordon
steps.text: ...You're goddamn right though.

steps.name: Gordon
steps.text: But... it's too late for me.

steps.name: Gordon
steps.text: Sorry.

steps.name: Glaucus
steps.text: For what?

steps.name: Gordon
steps.text: I mean... Sorry for that outburst just now. I got carried away.

steps.name: Glaucus
steps.text: Huh? I don't see anything wrong... Hm...

steps.name: Glaucus
steps.text: Mr. Gordon.

steps.name: Gordon
steps.text: Huh? What's the matter?

steps.name: Glaucus
steps.text: Do you use this weapon yourself?

steps.name: Gordon
steps.text: Yeah.

steps.name: Glaucus
steps.text: Your hands are injured, right? May I see them?

steps.name: Gordon
steps.text: ...Alright.
He presents a pair of timeworn hands. Under the light, his rough skin appears so dull that it is as if it is covered with a layer of ash.
On the back of each hand is a conspicuous scar resembling a valley in the desert.

steps.name: Gordon
steps.text: I only have my thumbs left. Can't move the others.

steps.name: Glaucus
steps.text: These calluses on your fingers... You're an outstanding mercenary, aren't you?

steps.name: Gordon
steps.text: Heh.

steps.name: Gordon
steps.text: A year ago, I got careless on a mission in Rim Billiton. Those bastards drove me into a corner, and they cut the tendons in my hands.

steps.name: Gordon
steps.text: I only have myself to blame for wasting all my money every payday. I had nothing saved up, and when it came time for my treatment, I had to take on an ass load of debt, and this is what I ended up with.

steps.name: Gordon
steps.text: ...Can't even pull a trigger. Now I need a toy crossbow like this to make a living and pay off my debts.

steps.name: Gordon
steps.text: A good-for-nothing like me's always gonna be down on his luck. In the end, even this toy is turning its back on me, making me watch, helpless... *spit*.

steps.name: Gordon
steps.text: Hah, but whatever. After today... it'll finally be over. Everything I should've ended a long time ago.

steps.name: Glaucus
steps.text: Um... If you don't mind, I have an idea.

steps.name: Glaucus
steps.text: I could help you modify your weapon to make it easier to use.

steps.name: Gordon
steps.text: Whatever works. Long as it shoots bolts when I need it to.

steps.name: Glaucus
steps.text: Alright.
Ten minutes later...

steps.name: Glaucus
steps.text: That should do it. Here.

steps.name: Gordon
steps.text: Is it good to go?

steps.name: Glaucus
steps.text: Well, I'm done modding it...

steps.name: Voice Outside the Door
steps.text: Who on Terra thought to hold a media day? What is even the point of these things? What a bunch of crap!

steps.name: Voice Outside the Door
steps.text: I have enough to worry about as it is. If it weren't for the recommendation, I wouldn't have even entertained interviewing anyone today.

steps.name: Gordon
steps.text: Is someone coming?!

steps.name: Glaucus
steps.text: That's probably Professor Millais.

steps.name: Gordon
steps.text: Quick! Give me the crossbow!

steps.name: Glaucus
steps.text: Huh? Wait!

steps.name: Glaucus
steps.text: I haven't told you how to use the new module yet—

steps.name: Millais
steps.text: Miss Glaucus.

steps.name: Millais
steps.text: Miss Glaucus!

steps.name: Glaucus
steps.text: Oh, sorry. You mentioned the practical exam, and it reminded me of what happened back then.

steps.name: Millais
steps.text: It's fine. My next...

steps.name: Glaucus
steps.text: Look at all the snacks you've got in this basket. Do you usually hold back from munching on them during interviews?

steps.name: Millais
steps.text: I'm... not a fan of snacks.

steps.name: Glaucus
steps.text: Is it okay I have a lollipop, then?

steps.name: Millais
steps.text: ...By all means.

steps.name: Millais
steps.text: My next question is, as all our research and development here is team-based, what do you think of group R&D?

steps.name: Glaucus
steps.text: You mean everyone here works as a team? That sounds pretty good to me.

steps.name: Glaucus
steps.text: When I worked at Rhodes Island, I often worked as a group, so I suppose I do have experience in that area.

steps.name: Millais
steps.text: When you worked with others before, did your team members say anything about your performance?

steps.name: Glaucus
steps.text: Oh, yes, they did. I think some of them said... uh...

steps.name: Glaucus
steps.text: That I should work on my own.

steps.name: Millais
steps.text: I have no more questions. Do you have any questions for me?

steps.name: Millais
steps.text: If not, then we'll...

steps.name: Glaucus
steps.text: (Hold on. Closure went over this. At the very end, when it's my turn to ask questions, I should ask the interviewer what they thought about me. That'll give me a good idea of whether I'll pass or not.)

steps.name: Glaucus
steps.text: So... what do you think about me?

steps.name: Millais
steps.text: (Deep breath)

steps.name: Millais
steps.text: You have proven your talent in engineering as a professional equipment designer.

steps.name: Millais
steps.text: Your answers in your field of expertise during the interview and your performance during the test were both practically perfect, and your ideas in the applications of electromagnets are very imaginative.

steps.name: Millais
steps.text: However, I find that your work habits and the direction of your research are somewhat different from what we have in mind.

steps.name: Millais
steps.text: For example, you insist on spending much of your energy on tuning and personalizing equipment, and it's reflected in your designs.

steps.name: Millais
steps.text: You customize your modules to the user's needs. This introduces complexities to the design, but the issues they are intended to address may very well be ones that the user could have gotten used to over time.

steps.name: Millais
steps.text: To tell you the truth, I don't think that's a bad thing, but when you design based around that logic, the additional costs don't result in additional profits. Furthermore, such designs cannot be produced on the assembly line.

steps.name: Millais
steps.text: In the end, Raythean Industries is a large corporation, and we aren't lacking in geniuses here.

steps.name: Millais
steps.text: Moreover, your work style is rather... unique. I'll have to think more about how well you'd perform in a team. That's more or less it.

steps.name: Glaucus
steps.text: Thank you.

steps.name: Millais
steps.text: Let's wrap it up here for today. All you need to do now is head home and wait for us to contact you. You may rest here for the time being. Someone from HR will escort you out later.

steps.name: Millais
steps.text: I have other things to attend to. Now if you'll excuse me.

steps.name: Glaucus
steps.text: Oh, okay.

steps.name: Millais
steps.text: Oh yes, and you may help yourself to the snacks in the basket.

steps.name: Glaucus
steps.text: (Sounds like this one's a bust. I guess I'll be helping Closure out for the foreseeable future.)

steps.name: Glaucus
steps.text: (Oh well. Heading back isn't so bad, but let me have something to eat first.)

steps.name: Glaucus
steps.text: Hm?

steps.name: Gordon
steps.text: Excuse me. I'm here to take out the garbage.

steps.name: Gordon
steps.text: You're...

steps.name: Glaucus
steps.text: It's you...

steps.name: Glaucus
steps.text: Oh, I get it.

steps.name: Glaucus
steps.text: They must've asked you to participate in my test this morning out of nowhere, right? Thank you for your work.

steps.name: Glaucus
steps.text: Your hands... Does it ever get in the way?

steps.name: Gordon
steps.text: I can still hold the tools I need to.

steps.name: Glaucus
steps.text: Oh, right. Your weapon...

steps.name: Gordon
steps.text: Shh, move.

steps.name: Gordon
steps.text: You have paper shreds next to you.

steps.name: Gordon
steps.text: Alright, my job here is done.

steps.name: Gordon
steps.text: Thanks for your help this morning. My dream has come true. From here on out, pretend like you've never seen me before.

steps.name: Gordon
steps.text: That's it. Goodbye.

steps.name: Glaucus
steps.text: Wait—

steps.name: Glaucus
steps.text: (That's strange... Wasn't he here this morning... to help evaluate me?)

steps.name: HR Employee
steps.text: Sorry for the wait. Let me walk you outside.

steps.name: Glaucus
steps.text: Oh, okay.

steps.name: HR Employee
steps.text: Right, we have a media day today. If you'd like, I could show you around our company's various departments.

steps.name: HR Employee
steps.text: This is our division's outdoor test site, and it's where we test out the capabilities of all the equipment and weapons we develop, and get the data for our designers to iterate upon.

steps.name: HR Employee
steps.text: The weapon you put together this morning was also tested here by our professionals. It was pretty well-received all around.

steps.name: Glaucus
steps.text: The weapon... Just one?

steps.name: HR Employee
steps.text: Yeah, that EMP field launcher. The idea of striking the enemy's tactical equipment was very creative. A couple of our senior designers in attendance were really inspired.

steps.name: HR Employee
steps.text: They all said that the last time they saw such an impressive design was when Professor Millais submitted his, right after he was reassigned here from HQ.

steps.name: Glaucus
steps.text: No way...

steps.name: HR Employee
steps.text: Can't imagine it, can you? Professor Millais is a genius, through and through. In just a few short years, he created multiple successful product lines for our division, and our profits saw a ten-fold growth.

steps.name: Glaucus
steps.text: No... That's not what I meant. What kind of tests do you normally give everyone who applies for the position?

steps.name: HR Employee
steps.text: Uh... I can't say.

steps.name: Glaucus
steps.text: Do they ever have to work with someone pretending to be a customer?

steps.name: HR Employee
steps.text: I can't recall anything like that happening...

steps.name: Glaucus
steps.text: Whoops, I may have, uh, presented myself as—

steps.name: HR Employee
steps.text: Oh, looks like the media tour's just made it here, too. And there's Professor Millais.

steps.name: HR Employee
steps.text: Let's wait here a little and let them head on over first.

steps.name: HR Employee
steps.text: Huh? Why is there still a janitor here? I thought they were going to have everything cleaned up before the media got here.

steps.name: Glaucus
steps.text: Mr. Gordon? That bag on his cart!

steps.name: Glaucus
steps.text: Stop that janitor!

steps.name: HR Employee
steps.text: What?

steps.name: Gordon
steps.text: It's too late...

steps.name: Glaucus
steps.text: Mr. Gordon!
At the very front of the group of visitors, the inconspicuous janitor suddenly removes his disguise and unleashes his original strength.
With everyone completely defenseless, none of them are able to escape the veteran mercenary's assault.
In a flash, he already has Professor Millais in a chokehold.

steps.name: Raythean Industries Security
steps.text: Emergency defense system activated!

steps.name: Gordon
steps.text: Don't move! If I see any of you move an inch, he's dead!

steps.name: Millais
steps.text: You hear him? Don't move!

steps.name: Gordon
steps.text: ...So fast to cave, huh?

steps.name: Raythean Industries Security
steps.text: Don't worry, Professor! You designed our defense system. It can shoot the hostage taker with no risk!

steps.name: Millais
steps.text: Shut up... Just do as he says!

steps.name: Millais
steps.text: *cough*... I had them stand down. They'll follow your orders. They do whatever I tell them anyway... So can you relax your grip a little? I can hardly breathe.

steps.name: Millais
steps.text: *cough*... You disguised yourself as a janitor and infiltrated us all this time, choosing this specific day to take me hostage... *cough*... instead of just killing me.

steps.name: Millais
steps.text: There's something you're after, isn't there?

steps.name: Gordon
steps.text: You're clever, I'll give you that.

steps.name: Millais
steps.text: Is it money? Or something else? Whatever it is, we can satisfy your demands.

steps.name: Gordon
steps.text: Good!

steps.name: Gordon
steps.text: Listen up, all of you! I have two demands!

steps.name: Gordon
steps.text: First, for Raythean Industries.

steps.name: Gordon
steps.text: Transfer 20 million Victorian pounds to the bank account on this strip of paper. Now!

steps.name: Millais
steps.text: Assistant. Bring me my terminal. I'll pay him with my personal account.

steps.name: Millais
steps.text: Immediately!

steps.name: Professor's Assistant
steps.text: Here, Professor.

steps.name: Millais
steps.text: ...Here's the receipt.

steps.name: Gordon
steps.text: Good. Efficient. That's a mega corp for you.

steps.name: Millais
steps.text: *cough*... I fulfilled your first demand. What's the other?

steps.name: Gordon
steps.text: My second demand is for all the members of the media in attendance!

steps.name: Millais
steps.text: What...?

steps.name: Gordon
steps.text: I want you all to report what I'm about to say, word for word.

steps.name: Raythean Industries Security
steps.text: He might very well damage our company's reputation! This could be a disaster!

steps.name: Raythean Industries Security
steps.text: Sorry, Professor! We have to activate the defense system. Trust us. It can handle threats of this level!

steps.name: Millais
steps.text: Wait! Don't do it!

steps.name: Raythean Industries Security
steps.text: Professor!

steps.name: Millais
steps.text: Dammit! That's a 'Raythean Navigator Mk. I' tactical crossbow! I'm the one who designed it!

spans.text: Dammit! That's a 'Raythean Navigator Mk. I' tactical crossbow! I'm the one who

steps.name: Millais
steps.text: It's controlled via multiple EMG sensors. It's 300 times faster than pulling the trigger by hand!

steps.name: Millais
steps.text: At this distance, if he wants to shoot me, the system won't stop him in time!

steps.name: Gordon
steps.text: So it was you...

steps.name: Gordon
steps.text: Hahahahaha.

steps.name: Millais
steps.text: What... What are you trying to say?

steps.name: Gordon
steps.text: I've been looking for this weapon's designer for a very long time.

steps.name: Gordon
steps.text: Everyone, I'm former specialist mercenary Gordon Bounou of Dakfung Security. I lost the use of my hands in an accident, so I was supplied a 'Raythean Navigator Mk. I' tactical crossbow.

steps.name: Gordon
steps.text: But I never expected that this half-baked, defective product would lead to an outcome I could never take back.

steps.name: Gordon
steps.text: Because it wouldn't shoot properly... I had no choice but to watch my... subordinate die...

steps.name: Millais
steps.text: Impossible...

steps.name: Gordon
steps.text: That account you just transferred the money into is his family's. That's what Raythean owes him! You have to take full responsibility for his death!

steps.name: Gordon
steps.text: Raythean Industries... this black-hearted company... and you, you bastard! For letting your unreliable weapons enter the market while you watch your stock prices go up from your offices...

steps.name: Gordon
steps.text: All of you assholes deserve to die!

steps.name: Gordon
steps.text: Too bad for you... No way I could've dealt with all of you, but looks like fate's on my side. I caught you.

steps.name: Millais
steps.text: Don't be hasty! There must be some kind of misunderstanding!

steps.name: Millais
steps.text: That weapon cannot be defective! I tested it myself!

steps.name: Gordon
steps.text: Shut up! I...

steps.name: Glaucus
steps.text: Try launching a bolt. Just give it a try.

steps.name: Millais
steps.text: What are you doing? Are you trying to get me killed?!

steps.name: Gordon
steps.text: Stay back! This has nothing to do with you!

steps.name: Glaucus
steps.text: No, I'm saying you should try firing your crossbow.

steps.name: Gordon
steps.text: Firing my...

steps.name: Gordon
steps.text: Right... I've come this far. There's no turning back.

steps.name: Gordon
steps.text: I lived half my life as a merc. I live and die by the crossbow... My life came to an end the day I lost the use of my hands.

steps.name: Gordon
steps.text: But now I have this bastard right here in my grip. If I can at least drag him down with me...

steps.name: Millais
steps.text: Wait! Don't do it!

steps.name: Glaucus
steps.text: ...Fire it.
Perhaps trying to look better in death, the man forces himself to smile, at least a little.
He contracts the muscles in his upper arm as he's practiced before, making no mistakes in the action.
In less than one three-hundredth of a second, the crossbow will fire, and its bolt will pierce his hostage's body.
Then, he will swallow the poison pill in his mouth, and everything will end exactly the way he envisioned.
Yet nothing happens.

steps.name: Gordon
steps.text: What... How come...?

steps.name: Millais
steps.text: Help!

steps.name: Raythean Industries Security
steps.text: Quick! Don't let him get away!

steps.name: Raythean Industries Security
steps.text: He's got something in his mouth! Open it up! Don't let him kill himself!
After a brief commotion, the crisis finally comes to an end.

steps.name: Gordon
steps.text: Get off me! Get off!

steps.name: Gordon
steps.text: No way... Why...? Why didn't it fire again?!

steps.name: Gordon
steps.text: What did you do? Didn't you say you fixed it?!

steps.name: Glaucus
steps.text: I didn't fix it, I modded it. To make it... suit you better.
She leans down and picks up the weapon that she modified herself.
The 'Returner.' That's the name she came up with for it.
She fastens the custom-made ringband that went ignored around her hand, and assumes a shooting stance.
Then, she pulls the trigger.

steps.name: Gordon
steps.text: This...

steps.name: Raythean Industries Security
steps.text: Don't move!

steps.name: Gordon
steps.text: Get off me! Let me see! Let me see her!

steps.name: Millais
steps.text: Relax your hold on him a little. Let him see... but don't let him go!

steps.name: Glaucus
steps.text: I was trying to tell you how to use it after I modded it, but I didn't get the chance.

steps.name: Glaucus
steps.text: After seeing your hands, I figured that as a veteran, pulling the trigger has to be the action you're most familiar with, right?

steps.name: Glaucus
steps.text: You've been on thousands of missions and come back from danger countless times, so I knew that being able to shoot accurately and instinctively has to be the one thing you can count on the most.

steps.name: Glaucus
steps.text: So when I saw that you can still move your thumb, I made a little change.

steps.name: Glaucus
steps.text: Instead of relying on the EMG sensor, I added a ringband that stands in for the trigger being pulled.

steps.name: Glaucus
steps.text: That way, you can pull the trigger yourself and fire your crossbow the way you're most familiar with.

steps.name: Glaucus
steps.text: Professor, is it alright if we let him try it?

steps.name: Millais
steps.text: ...Keep him under control.

steps.name: Glaucus
steps.text: Here, put this on. Give it a try.

steps.name: Glaucus
steps.text: How is it? Not bad, huh?
There is no answer.
He simply lets the tears in his eyes run down his face.

steps.name: Professor's Assistant
steps.text: Professor, the results of the investigation are in.

steps.name: Professor's Assistant
steps.text: A mercenary called Gordon did indeed use our 'Raythean Navigator Mk. I' during a mission. It was bought wholesale by Dakfung Security for their disabled soldiers.

steps.name: Professor's Assistant
steps.text: And the mission did turn out as he said. Six months ago, a 23 years old mercenary was killed by rioters because the man wasn't able to fire his weapon in time.

steps.name: Professor's Assistant
steps.text: After the incident, he left Dakfung Security and used one of the fake identities he used as a mercenary to apply to become a janitor at our division.

steps.name: Professor's Assistant
steps.text: He'd been planning this for a very long time. He was going to commit suicide during our media day, and lay all the blame on our company.

steps.name: Professor's Assistant
steps.text: Since we outsourced janitorial work to a service company, we didn't discover his plan in time. This oversight is our security department's responsibility, and we'll make sure that they take the necessary precautions going forward.

steps.name: Millais
steps.text: Necessary precautions... If it weren't for that candidate modifying his weapon, I would've been killed!

steps.name: Professor's Assistant
steps.text: I'm truly sorry!

steps.name: Millais
steps.text: Never mind... Did you bring the report regarding the mission he was on?

steps.name: Professor's Assistant
steps.text: Here it is.

steps.name: Millais
steps.text: Did the 'Navigator Mk. I' really malfunction...?

steps.name: Professor's Assistant
steps.text: Based on the operational logs we exported from the unit, it seems... it was working as intended.

steps.name: Professor's Assistant
steps.text: And Dakfung Security's internal investigation report shows that the real reason behind that incident was that the mercenary subconsciously wanted to pull the trigger...

steps.name: Millais
steps.text: ...and failed.

steps.name: Professor's Assistant
steps.text: It's a good thing he didn't get his way. I mean, I knew there could never be a problem with your design.

steps.name: Millais
steps.text: No.

steps.name: Millais
steps.text: Announce to the public that his weapon malfunctioned and caused the accident. That we sincerely regret this and will take full responsibility.

steps.name: Professor's Assistant
steps.text: What? Professor!

steps.name: Millais
steps.text: Now leave, and do as I said. I'll pay for any compensation out of my own pocket.

steps.name: Professor's Assistant
steps.text: Understood.

steps.name: Millais
steps.text: Phew...

steps.name: Millais
steps.text: That's fine with you, right boss?
Mhm.
Is there anything else you want to say?

steps.name: Millais
steps.text: Of course, I also wanted to talk to you about the new candidate, Glaucus. Didn't you contact me because of her?

steps.name: Millais
steps.text: She may have saved my life, but my judgment is still that she's not fit to be an equipment designer.

steps.name: Millais
steps.text: Her design philosophy simply can't develop the sort of products that could expand our company or increase our profit margins.
I know.

steps.name: Millais
steps.text: But she is indeed a genius, and your headquarters can't let talents like her slip by.

I will send someone to sign a cooperation agreement with her and sign her on as a advanced weapon evaluator. She will be in charge of tuning the latest weapons, and all the company's most innovative research will be made available to her.

steps.name: Millais
steps.text: Good. That's a much better position for her.
'A technology company should strive to better serve the masses with technology.' I remember you saying that during your interview, years ago.

steps.name: Millais
steps.text: Right. I wonder how I turned out the way I am now.

steps.name: Millais
steps.text: When I interviewed Glaucus, I asked her the same question. How she sees the relationship between technology and people.

steps.name: Millais
steps.text: And her answer was...

steps.name: Millais
steps.text: 'Technology may have forged my legs, but it's only when I run that they have meaning.'
